newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica JSE turnover up 76.6 pct in first 7 months.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica JSE turnover up 76.6 pct in first 7 months.

text.p: Turnover on South Africa's Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), excluding arbitrage deals, surged 76.6 percent in the first seven months of the year compared to the same period last year, the bourse said on Wednesday.
The JSE said trade worth 113.28 billion rand had been concluded from the start of the year to July 31, compared with 64.15 billion in the same period last year.
Net foreign purchases in the first seven months of 1997 stood at 13.17 billion rand compared to 5.25 billion rand for the whole of 1996.
Market capitalisation rose 19.1 percent to 1,304 billion rand in the seven months to July compared to 1,095 billion rand in the same period in 1996.

In U.S. dollar terms the JSE's market capitalisation was worth $279.67 billion on June 30, 1997. It ranks as the 18th largest bourse in the world by dollar market capitalisation among the 45 member stock exchanges of the Federation Internationale des Bourses de Valeurs.
In July 1997 liquidity improved to 18.3 percent from 8.7 percent in the same month last year, a change of 110.3 percent.
The JSE's liquidity ratio in dollar terms on June 30 was 14.7 percent, ranking it 39th.
